notIdeasOfWhatSocietyShouldBe.explanation: The Communards are defined entirely by an event: the members and supporters of the 1871 Paris Commune. Looking through the statements, the Commune's decrees do answer some (separation of church and state, abolition of the death penalty and conscription, workers' right to take over abandoned enterprises, self-policing), so this is not an entry without ideas; but those are the Commune's record as an event, one government of two months made up of Jacobins, Blanquists, Proudhonists and members of the International, and no source names a doctrine of the Communards themselves. The ideas belong to the Paris Commune, socialism, communalism and the other ideologies its participants held, and the entry has only the event's participants.
